claims.text: The starting material is CoCrFeNi without engineered secondary phases.
Laser surface alloying or a similar treatment can incorporate a small, uniformly distributed nanoscale silver addition into the top few microns of CoCrFeNi.
The surface treatment will facilitate segregation of the added element to the sliding interface.
The added silver will oxidize at the sliding interface as temperature increases.
Interfacial oxidation will produce a continuous, fine-grained lubricious silver-oxide or mixed high-entropy-oxide tribolayer.
The oxide tribolayer will act as both a protective barrier and a lubricant.
At lower temperatures, the modified surface will retain a stable microstructure while the additive remains inert.
At elevated temperatures, the tribolayer formed from the dispersed additive will be self-healing.
The tribolayer will minimize adhesive interactions during sliding.
The tribolayer will reduce abrasive wear.
Compared with untreated CoCrFeNi, the modified surface will have a lower coefficient of friction at every tested temperature from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
Compared with untreated CoCrFeNi, the modified surface will have a lower wear rate at every tested temperature from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
The largest friction and wear improvements will occur at high temperatures because oxidative tribolayer formation is activated there.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi has difficulty maintaining low friction and wear consistently from room temperature to 800 °C.
Extreme loads may compromise formation or retention of the lubricious layer.
Non-oxidative environments may compromise the intervention's benefits.
Rapid thermal cycling may compromise formation or retention of the lubricious layer.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes low friction and wear over the full temperature range to a continuous oxide tribolayer, but the mechanism says that at lower temperatures the additive remains inert and that oxidative tribolayer formation is activated only as temperature increases. No alternative room-temperature lubrication mechanism is provided.
